body:
Edit image 1, the BODY UV texture atlas, in place. Image 2 is ONLY an art direction reference: match the middle column B, bold comic ink, on the atlas surfaces. OUTPUT ONLY the square atlas, never a character illustration or comparison sheet.
CRITICAL UV constraints: Preserve the exact image dimensions/aspect, background, island silhouettes, every island coordinate, padding and orientation from image 1. Do NOT rearrange, resize, add, remove, merge or rotate islands. Keep all facial eye/eyebrow coordinates, hairline shapes, badge and patch positions pixel-aligned. Existing head faces, rust-red cap panels, teal jacket, charcoal blue pants, brown boots, skin hands/neck retain their base colors. Preserve return-home cap badge, beige crown repair, rust sleeve patch, teal trouser repair.
Make a visibly strong COMIC BOOK inked texture version, not the subtle painted original. Bold confident dark colored ink contours around ACTUAL garment constructions: cap panel seams, brim edge, pocket flap/side/bottom, central zipper, cuffs, pant hems, shoe sole and panels. At this approx 1254 atlas size use primary construction strokes roughly 4-6px, secondary folds 2-3px; sparse tapering angular crease strokes only where sleeves bend and garments compress. Lines are clean and dark enough to read at small top-down game size. No thin scratchy wireframe, no random all-over hatching. Do not outline every UV island perimeter indiscriminately: those cuts are often arbitrary surfaces, not physical seams. Preserve 4-6px matching base-color bleed outside islands, no black padding borders.
Replace all polygonal camouflage/brush mottling with 2-3 clean opaque contiguous color values per material and a few large graphic folded shapes. Matte albedo without highlights, specular, glowing edges, AO gradients or directional lighting baked in. Cap stitching can be few broken dark lines, brim seam should be bold. Jacket pockets strong near-black teal line around flap and pocket, clean teal flat fields. Pants sparse dark navy creases and clear hems. Shoes dark umber constructed panel lines. Hair same shape but simplify to a few dark grouped locks. FACE/SKIN should remain simple clean original with same eyes, no new wrinkles/beard/mouth/nose/eyelashes or outline around arbitrary face-UV seams; remove subtle cheek scratches. Preserve all small skin islands clean.
Aim for the character to look ink-drawn when mapped onto the existing mesh, matching B interior clothing linework. No new geometry, no text labels, no watermark, no background artwork.
bodyBoundaryCleanup:
Precise technical cleanup of THIS UV atlas; output same square atlas with EVERY island position/shape/size unchanged. Preserve ALL internal comic ink lines, dark construction seams, illustrated folds, garment pockets, colors, repair patches, cap badge, facial eyes/eyebrows and the shape of the hairline.
Remove ONLY the black perimeter outlines that trace the outside edge of the separate UV islands. In particular ALL skin head islands, ALL skin hands/neck islands, all jacket and trouser panel exterior perimeters, all separate cap and shoe island outer perimeters. Replace that outer contour stroke with the immediately adjacent INSIDE fill color and extend that fill color 5 pixels outward into padding. Do not leave a dark halo. These polygons are UV cuts and their borders must have colored bleed, not ink: on the mapped 3D model black UV borders would draw unwanted seams across faces and arms.
The actual INSIDE drawn seams on cap panels, cuffs and hems, front pockets, zipper, cap brim construction and shoe soles MUST remain richly inked. This task removes arbitrary boundary strokes, not actual interior garment construction linework. Hairline separating hair and skin remains. All eyes and internal illustration details unchanged. Background remains dark neutral. No layout moves, no texture redesign, no flattening of current bold comic style. Preserve original pixel alignment.
gearAfterShadowApproval:
Edit image 1 GEAR UV atlas in place. Image 2 is BODY texture only as matching comic ink/color treatment reference. Image 3 is concept art direction; middle B chosen. Output ONLY the first square gear atlas, same exact dimensions, all island silhouettes, coordinates and sizes. No illustrations or comparison sheet.
Replace soft painterly mottling with confident bold COMIC linework and clean cel-like 2-3-step colored SHADOW SHAPES PAINTED DIRECTLY INTO THE TEXTURE. User expressly wants drawn shadows as personality. Put bold warm dark-umber graphic shadow bands under backpack flap, buckles and folded corners; decisive deep orange angular scarf fold shadows, clean bright orange fields; ochre waist charm solid yellow and dark gold shadow planes. NOT glossy, no photographic fabric, no tiny scratches.
Make actual pocket/flap border, construction seams, leather belt edges and buckle boldly inked (3-5px equivalent on this1254 atlas), secondary few creases2px, occasional short hatch group only deep folded corner. Matching comic B: sharp purposeful graphic surfaces that read at small top-down view. Broader flat tan-brown backpack fields, strongly inked rectangular flap and buckle on lower-right large panel. Preserve the small chalk return-home arrow and rust stitched patch EXACTLY where present, same shape. Keep all existing buckle, strap, scarf, charm contents, no new gear/motifs. Leather stays dark brown, tan canvas stays brown, scarf orange not red.
UV safety: absolutely no island moves/repacking/resizing/additions. The FIRST reference is the editing target and sole layout authority. The black/dark background stays. DO NOT put a dark contour around every separate UV polygon: arbitrary UV borders must have same local fill color bleed 5px outwards. Only real construction seams/internal fabric folds have ink. Do not outline scarf arbitrary cut surfaces. Preserve exactly the original all island perimeter silhouettes and extents. Body reference is style ONLY, do not put faces/caps/clothes on gear sheet. No labels or watermark.
note: User subsequently explicitly approved graphic shadows painted into textures. Final body already contains graphic value shapes; gear prompt incorporates this decision.
